newsitem.title: USA: AOL stock slumps after competition warning.
newsitem.headline: AOL stock slumps after competition warning.

text.p: America Online Inc. stock slumped Tuesday after the company's latest warning that other online services and direct Internet access providers could spell tougher competition in future.
The stock fell $3.75 to $31.75 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most active issues.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, AOL reiterated comments it made to analysts last quarter, warning of potentially high "churn" rates, the rate at which new customers join and leave the service.
Some analysts expressed surprise at the stock's fall, saying there was nothing new in the filing to merit a sell-off.
"(Investors) are significantly overreacting," said Abhishek Gami, an analyst for Nesbitt Burns.
"AOL may surprise all these people ... They have already confirmed the churn (rate) improved in this quarter and with the new marketing push, I'm convinced it will improve further," Gami said.
The company said Monday it will spend more than $100 million in a new marketing campaign targeted to personal computer owners who are not current AOL members.
America Online is due to report earnings for its first fiscal quarter ended Sept. 30 in late October or early November. It usually includes churn rate details in its quarterly announcements.
